content: The Washington Hospital Center, a member of MedStar Health, is a not-for-profit institution licensed for 926 beds and typically operates near full capacity. It provides a comprehensive range of primary, secondary, and tertiary care services to both adult and neonatal patients. The hospital is situated on a 47-acre campus in Northwest Washington, which it shares with three other medical facilities. Adjacent to the hospital are the National Rehabilitation Hospital and the Children’s National Medical Center, the latter of which also operates satellite centers throughout the city. The Washington Heart program is nationally recognized for its leadership in cardiovascular disease research, diagnosis, and treatment. Its cardiac catheterization laboratory is the busiest in the United States, as acknowledged by the DuPont Foundation. The hospital performed one of the first heart transplants in the Washington area on May 22, 1987. Beyond cardiac care, the hospital is highly regarded for its expertise in oncology, neurosciences, gastrointestinal disorders, endocrinology, women’s health, transplantation, and burn care. The hospital’s neurosciences program offers a full spectrum of surgical and minimally invasive treatments and operates the only JCAHO-accredited Primary Stroke Center in the District. Its adult burn center is the most advanced in the region. The Washington Cancer Institute (WCI) is the largest cancer care provider in the District, diagnosing over 2,580 new cases and managing more than 84,299 outpatient visits and 2,423 inpatient admissions in fiscal year 2006. WCI provides interdisciplinary care, including surgical, radiation, and medical oncology services, as well as patient and family counseling, cancer education, community outreach, and clinical research trials. The Center for Breast Health alone treated approximately 15,358 patients in fiscal year 2006. The hospital’s transplantation program ranks in the top five percent nationally for patient outcomes, consistently exceeding the national average. Its kidney, pancreas, and heart transplantation services are among the busiest on the East Coast. The MedSTAR Transport air ambulance service, operational since 1983, had transported 40,293 patients by 2007. The MedSTAR Trauma program is consistently recognized by the American College of Surgeons as one of the nation’s premier Level I shock/trauma units. The Washington Hospital Center was established in March 1958 through the merger of three specialty hospitals. On May 7, 1998, its parent company, Medlantic Healthcare Group, merged with Helix Health, a Baltimore-based hospital group, forming the largest healthcare provider in the mid-Atlantic region. The combined entity was renamed MedStar Health on February 1, 1999. In fiscal year 2006, the hospital served 46,155 inpatients, including 4,409 births, and 366,248 outpatients. Its medical and dental staff comprised 1,584 professionals. During the same period, 19,054 cardiac catheterizations, 1,803 open-heart surgeries, and six heart transplants were performed. Additionally, 111 kidney transplants, four combined kidney/pancreas transplants, and three pancreas transplants were conducted. The hospital also managed 3,791 helicopter transports and 1,007 trauma unit visits. The Emergency Department recorded 74,025 visits, including 18,776 admissions. The hospital provided $3 million in charity care during fiscal year 2006. The hospital was the only one in Washington to be ranked in the areas of heart and heart surgery, geriatrics, and kidney disease and transplantation in U.S. News & World Report’s 18th annual survey of 5,462 healthcare facilities. The rankings were based on reputation, mortality rates, and patient care-related factors, including nursing and patient services. The hospital’s proprietary Azyxxi healthcare software gained attention when it was acquired by Microsoft in July 2006.
